title: Sequence stratification and amortized padding scheduler
text:
Sequence stratification and amortized padding scheduler

description:
Background: We observe high padding overhead for mixed sequence-length traffic during prefill and decode phases. Rather than classic rigid bucketing, this ticket introduces a lightweight sequence stratification layer plus an amortized padding scheduler that reduces effective padding by sharing padding budget across near-length requests and by deferring non-critical prefill consolidation into short amortization windows. The goal is to reduce padded tokens and overall GPU token cost without increasing p99 latency or kernel thrashing.

Scope: implement a stratifier that groups incoming requests into 3 dynamic strata (short/medium/long) based on running seqlen histograms and variance; implement an amortization window (configurable ms) that allows small hold-and-merge windows for compatible requests; integrate scheduler with kernel-selection hints (prefer small-seq optimized kernels for short strata, fused attention kernels for medium strata, streaming attention for long strata); expose runtime flags and metrics in Console. This ticket covers design, prototype in the dev runtime, and a small-scale canary.


proposal:
High-level approach: 1) Add a lightweight strata classifier in the front of the prefill queue that uses recent seqlen quantiles (10/50/90) to compute dynamic cutpoints. 2) Maintain three in-memory queues (strata) with separate short amortization windows: short window=6ms, medium window=12ms, long window=0ms (no wait). 3) When a window closes, apply an amortized padding strategy: compute target pad length equal to the 95th percentile length inside the amortized batch, then allow a per-request slack factor to avoid skewing latency. 4) Emit kernel-hint metadata to the runtime scheduler for per-batch kernel selection and attention path (e.g., prefuse, split-attn, causal-stream). 5) Fall back to immediate dispatch when latency SLOs are threatened.

Why different: We call this amortized padding because we allow a short, bounded delay to aggregate similar requests and amortize padding overhead, instead of rigid size buckets which often cause memory fragmentation and kernel underutilization. The stratifier is adaptive (cutpoints move every 30s) so it adapts to traffic shifts without manual tuning.


acceptance_criteria:
Padded token reduction >= 18% across representative mixed workloads (chat + long form) measured over 1h
No more than 5% regressive change in p99 tail latency for the API route under baseline 99th percentile workload
GPU tokens/sec improves or remains flat with amortization enabled (no throughput regression > 3%)
Kernel change rate (number of distinct kernel switches per minute) does not increase > 20% compared to current baseline
Console exposes metrics: strata counts, amortization wait histogram, pad tokens saved, kernel-hint distribution

tasks:
Design proto: strata algorithm and cutpoint heuristics (Aisha)
Implement strata classifier and amortization windows in prefill queue (Tomás)
Add kernel-hint metadata and adapt scheduler to consume hints (Liam)
Instrument metrics and Console dashboard (Observability team)
Run benchmarks with synthetic and sampled production traces (perf team)
Canary rollout and rollback automation (SRE)

experiment_results:
Synthetic mix (30% short, 50% medium, 20% long) on A100: padded token reduction 21.4%, tokens/sec +2.1%, p99 latency +0.6% (within target)
Sampled prod trace (regional small): padded token reduction 16.9% on g4dn, but kernel-change rate +28% under naively aggressive cutpoints
Tuning window: reducing medium window from 20ms->12ms reduced kernel-change rate back below 15% while keeping pad reduction ~18%
KV cache reuse improvements observed for medium strata when amortization window kept <15ms (fewer mid-request cache flushes)

notes:
We purposely avoid creating many rigid buckets because previous attempts led to inefficient kernel packing and GPU memory fragmentation.
The 95th percentile pad target was chosen after exploring mean and median targets; p95 balances pad reduction and tail latency for the workloads tested.
Amortization windows are configurable per-route and can be disabled for low-latency premium routes.
We must ensure that function-calling/structured-output traces with multi-turn prefills treat the amortization across turns carefully to avoid cross-request contamination.

risks:
Holding requests introduces extra request latency; mitigated by short windows and SLO-aware immediate dispatch path.
Aggressive stratification may increase kernel churn; we add hysteresis to cutpoint movement to avoid thrashing.
Complexity in KV cache lifetime when batches mix requests with overlapping conversation IDs; added guard: do not merge requests with shared conversation state unless explicit safe flag present.

rollout_plan:
Dev deploy: feature gated behind runtime flag and test harness (done)
Canary: 1% traffic in us-west for 48h with pad and latency dashboards monitored (next step)
Expand to 10% with automated rollback trigger: pad-savings <10% OR p99 regression >5% for 30m
Full rollout: 100% after 2 successful days at 10% and stakeholder signoff

comments:
2025-02-12 Aisha Kapoor: Initial design sketch uploaded to Confluence and linked above. Chosen to target three strata to keep overhead minimal.
2025-02-20 Tomás Rivera: Prototype implemented in dev runtime. Basic metrics plumbing added. Early experiments show promising pad reduction but kernel-change rate is sensitive to cutpoint tuning.
2025-02-27 Liam Chen: Kernel-hint API merged. Scheduler accepts hint strings 'short-opt','mid-fused','long-stream' and uses them to bias kernel selection. Observed better packing for mid fused kernels.
2025-03-02 Perf team: Ran larger sample using 24h production trace subset. Pad reduction averaged 19% and throughput improved slightly; flagged rare cases where amortization increased p99 by ~8% under bursty arrival patterns. We added burst detection bypass.
2025-03-04 Tomás Rivera: Tuned medium window and added hysteresis to cutpoint updates. Prepared canary runbook and updated acceptance gating. Assigned SRE for canary monitoring.
